subject: Post-demo: recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps
messages:
From: Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.ai>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-06-10T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Post-demo: recommended models, benchmarks, and next steps

Thanks again for the time today, Sam — good discussion. Quick recap and specific next steps so we keep momentum: 

Summary from our call
- Primary goal: generate compact, customer-facing summaries from transaction logs (~400–800 tokens) with high factuality and <300ms P50 generation in production.
- Secondary: embeddings for semantic search (monthly 20M requests).

Initial model-fit recommendations (based on the training prompts + latency targets)
- Candidate A: LlamaX-27B-chat (8k context) — best quality/throughput balance for your summarization prompts.
- Candidate B: Redwood-7B-q4f — lower cost option with comparable recall on short summaries; we expect slightly higher variance on edge-cases.

What I attached/linked
- redwood-performance-profiles.csv (summary of verified TPS & latency percentiles across variants)
- prompt-sets-automation.docx (your demo prompts + our scoring prompts)
- perf dashboard link (console) and a short runbook below.

Key sanity checks we need from ClearPath
1) A representative sample of 150-200 anonymized transactions (redact PII) so we can run our quality/regression evals.
2) Confirmation on target SLAs (P50 <300ms; P95 <850ms OR willingness to accept ~1s for tail).

Suggested next steps
- If you’re comfortable, I’ll schedule a 60-min technical deep-dive with Neha to go over batching/quantization and a timeline for the eval run (target: 72 hours after we get samples).
- We’ll populate a mutual action plan and I can share a draft PO/quote after we agree on deployment mode (hosted vs dedicated).

References
- Redwood-verified profiles: https://redwood.ai/perf/rdw-1234
- Perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/clearpath-87

Thanks — I’ll follow up with proposed times for the deep-dive.

— Priyom
Priyom Das | Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference

Thanks Sam — good questions. Short answers + links below.

P50/P95 context
- The numbers in redwood-performance-profiles.csv are measured on Redwood-hosted instances (multi-tenant but with dedicated runtime slices). For dedicated pools we see ~10–20% lower median/95th tail depending on GPU class and batch config.
- Example verified numbers (LlamaX-27B-chat, 2k token cap, contin. batching enabled): P50=0.28s, P95=0.72s under 75 TPS sustained. See perf dashboard: https://console.redwood.ai/perf/clearpath-87

Hallucination mitigation / eval suite
- Neha and team run a 3-stage eval: unit prompt QA -> adversarial prompt injection -> real-sample regression check. We tag regressions by severity and run human review for high-severity drift.
- We’ve added a small example eval set to the Drive folder: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1examplePromptSet

Cost/commitment (ballpark)
- Hosted: ~$0.018 / 1k tokens (inference) + $0.003 / embedding request (these are example numbers, final pricing depends on tokens/throughput).
- Dedicated (monthly reserved): commit tiers start at $12k/mo (small pool) with discounts at 3–12 month terms; dedicated gives tighter P95 guarantees.

Next steps
- If OK, I’ll schedule the deep-dive with Neha (45–60m) to walk technical design and we’ll run the 72-hour eval once we get the samples.

I’ll add Neha to the thread for the technical deep-dive slot.

— Priyom

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.ai>

Hi Sam / Priyom — quick tech notes ahead of the deep-dive so we can use time efficiently: 

Technical hints / what we’ll validate in the 72-hr eval
- Batching & concurrency: target steady-state 50–80 TPS for summaries; use small concurrency (3–5 concurrent requests) with continuous batching to hit P50 targets.
- KV cache: enable prefix K/V caching on repeat customers to cut token compute >20% for conversational flows.
- Quantization: Redwood-7B-q4f recommended for cost-constrained workloads; for LlamaX-27B-chat we recommend q5_0 mixed precision for best quality/latency tradeoff.
- Quality/regression tooling: we’ll run EVAL-CP-2026-01 (labelled test set) and track MRR/factuality/ROUGE-like metrics; high-severity regressions trigger a rollback to the previous model variant per our rollout policy.

Attachments I uploaded:
- prompt-sets-automation.docx (annotated prompts + scoring rubric)
- clearpath-integration-mapping.xlsx (example transformation mapping we discussed)

Operational notes
- If you choose dedicated, we’ll pre-provision a small pool (cc: Dev to coordinate infra sizing).
- Let us know if you require KMS/HSM for key management — we support both in Private deployments.

I’m available for the technical deep-dive tomorrow at 10:00 or 14:00 PT. Which works for you, Sam?

— Neha
